lead_headline: Foreclosure filings surge 40% week-over-week to 42 while restaurant tracker idles at 55 active leads—Sunday's twin Dairy Queen closures offset by zero new openings

restaurant.blurb: 2 new leads today—both closures—lift active count to 55 total (26 openings, 29 closures). Sunday's detections: Dairy Queen Grill & Chill in Fort Logan (2897 W Belleview, Littleton, recently shuttered per March Yelp updates) and identical Westminster location flagged as duplicate. Opening side holds flat at 26 despite week's robust activity: Mendocino Farms' Highland debut Monday, Vaultaire's subterranean HiFi lounge beneath La Forêt Tuesday, FiNO Mediterranean at All Inn Hotel Wednesday. Closure roster climbs to 29 with Super Mega Bien's permanent close (Five Points, 8-year fixture ended March 14), Aspen Baking Company's sudden shutdown (Stapleton wholesaler ceased operations March 6 mid-acquisition). Geographic spread: Union Station captures four openings week-to-date (G-Que BBQ, Mendocino Farms, C Burger, Ogo Korean), Regis logs three closures (303 Ramen fire, two Dairy Queen exits). Closure margin widens to 3-lead gap—tightest opening-closure parity since February erodes as detection pace favors shutdowns.

foreclosure.blurb: 42 new filings this week vault 40% above prior week's 30—sharpest single-week acceleration since late January shatters March's early softness. 104 auctions scheduled next seven days (down marginally from 106 midweek) sustain near-term pipeline, but $71M total exposure compresses as mega-filing drought persists—only one seven-figure case this week ($795K Weld County property) vs January's routine $1M+ clusters. Arapahoe's $57M South Vaughn outlier dominates value calculations but reflects commercial distress, not residential volume. County standings: El Paso leads at 475 active, Weld climbs to 431, Arapahoe holds 451. March volatility intensifies—30-72 filing weekly range replaces January's predictable 50+ cadence as baseline fractures into boom-bust rhythm. Seven-day filing surge signals distress acceleration, not data artifact.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention today holds seven-day total at 47 citations across 11 sources—up 7% from prior week's 44, snapping two-week slide. Denver Post dominates with 22 pickups (47% share, up from 45%), social platforms deliver 13 mentions (Instagram 8, Facebook 5), Hoodline trails at 4. Saturday's lone detection: Denver Post tax-focused page. Week's top stories: Kwame Spearman/Denver Book Society split (Hoodline pickup), PharmaCann cannabis layoffs (Post), Thriving Families HQ purchase (Post), Cheesman Park penthouse listing (Post). Source concentration tightens: Post plus social command 74% of weekly volume—single-outlet dependency remains structural risk as niche publishers contribute sporadically. Discovery stays 100% Google News RSS. Monthly pace: 131 mentions through 22 days projects 175-mention March if sustained, tracking 34% above February's final tally.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +0 yesterday (0 new, 0 canceled) leaves MTD at +34 (+1.6/day), 90-day cumulative at +103. Saturday's idle marks third zero-net day this month but follows Friday's +3 performance—weekend volatility typical. Seven-day window: +17 net (23 new, 6 canceled) exactly matches prior week's +17, fourth consecutive week holding 15-17 net band. Acquisition steadies at 3-4 daily baseline post-March 9's 8-new outlier, cancellations compress to 0.9/day vs March average of 1.4/day. March's 1.6/day rate tracks 23% above YTD's 1.3/day benchmark—strongest sustained monthly performance year-to-date. Recent pattern: three-week stabilization after early-month churn, new subscriber flow normalizes at 3-5 daily, cancellation floor settles near 1/day. Sunday's flat reading non-alarming given weekend acquisition lull.
